correctness.rationale: Every bounded Eulerian rank-three poset has a 2-regular bipartite atom-coatom incidence graph. Partition into even cycle components is exact by degree-two structure and rank preservation. All strict-order atomic pair counts depend only on rank and r, giving complete C^2 theory equivalence by induction on two-variable counting formulas. Three-variable repeated squaring expresses component membership up to radius r in ceil(log2 r) steps and component-count quantifiers identify the exact partition at quantifier rank <=ceil(log2 r)+3. Two atoms have two common coatoms iff a C4 component exists, giving precisely nonlattices. Side-preserving cyclic automorphisms yield 2+2s orbits, and the extremal/partition formulas follow by explicit bijections. There is no missing infinite computation or appeal to empirical extrapolation. Two standalone programs were rerun and matched their saved outputs exactly: a 230-type full check through r=16 and an exhaustive independent incidence matrix enumeration through r=5 (1,6,90,2040 labelled incidence matrices). Finite tests are secondary evidence only.

value.rationale: A natural foundational family (rank-three Eulerian posets) has a strong complete profile: finite-variable counting logic fails to see genuine latticehood at the sharp 10-element boundary and orbit cells at the sharp 12-element boundary, whereas three counting variables reconstruct the exact cycle partition with logarithmic quantifier rank. The same partition determines all isomorphism, lattice, nonlattice, refinability and maximal-orbit counts and proves an unbounded automorphism-orbit gap inside one full C^2 theory at each size. This is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary isolated numerical improvement. The literature-known structural decomposition and generic logic theory are explicitly credited; no downstream application is presumed.
